analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. The visible patch excerpts change docs/reference/configuration.md and docs/reference/provider-authorization.md. No executable code, protocol, key handling or authorization logic changes.

configuration.md: the head text units cover lines 315-739 (model cache, engine/scheduler env vars, SSD prefix cache, memory budgets). The file changes show only these edits:
- Lines 5-7: the intro drops "retained-console" wording and attributes console settings to the platform configuration reference.
- Base lines 84-99: the Console UI env-var section is removed, including the NEXT_PUBLIC_* table.

The retained text I reviewed is unchanged context. It describes the SSD prefix cache (T-041), including the 1800s TTL ceiling, the debug-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE, and the ephemeral-KEK opt-ins. It also describes the model cache location, the LaunchAgent env allow-list and the EnvironmentScrubber. I found no contradiction with the T-041 mitigations or with TB-003/TB-007. Documented defaults, such as a 30-minute TTL that env vars can only shorten, match the threat model. Scope is narrower than the base, so there is no new attack surface.

provider-authorization.md: the date bump to 2026-10-27 and the removal of the console-ui path reference. The text now says the MDM deactivation notice sets no retirement date and does not disable legacy serving, which is consistent with T-052, T-054 and T-057. The console is out of scope for the provider threat model, so removing it does not invalidate any assumption.

I could not see the full patch excerpt for the Console UI removal, since it is truncated, but the range map is complete and shows only deletions. Remaining integration question: none material. The documented behaviors were not checked against source, which is outside the supplied evidence.
